data.text: **Question:** What is the difference between value types and reference types?
Value types store data directly on the stack and are copied when assigned. Reference types store a reference to heap memory and share the same object.

Value types (int, bool, struct) are stored on stack, copied on assignment. Reference types (class, string, array) store reference on stack, actual data on heap. Affects memory management and performance.
